title: ⚠️ CAUTION ADVISED — Urea on Rice at Flowe...

messages.text:
⚠️ CAUTION ADVISED — Urea on Rice at Flowering Stage in Ahmedabad:

Current conditions: 29.3°C, 72% humidity, 20% rain probability, 9mm forecasted rain in 48h.

Agronomic assessment:
• Your rice is in the CRITICAL 'Flowering & Grain Development' stage (Day 25–60 of the 120-day cycle).
• Top-dressing urea during flowering is generally NOT recommended — excess nitrogen now causes excessive vegetative growth, lodging, and poor grain filling (chaffy grains).
• If leaves show clear nitrogen deficiency (pale yellow, especially older leaves), a VERY light split dose of 5–8 kg urea/acre can be applied, incorporated into moist soil, preferably before the 9mm rain window.
• With 20% rain probability, immediate washout risk is low, but 9mm incoming rain could cause minor leaching — apply early morning (6–8 AM) so roots can uptake before night.
• HIGH RISK: Bacterial Leaf Blight probability is 62% — urea-driven lush growth attracts vectors. Monitor for water-soaked lesions on leaf tips.

Better option: Switch to Potassium Sulfate (0-0-50) @ 10 kg/acre during grain filling to improve grain quality and blast resistance.

If you confirm nitrogen deficiency, apply urea in a 1% foliar spray (1 kg urea + 100L water + 1g surfactant) for safer, targeted uptake without soil leaching.

personaAdvisory.title: FARMER DIRECTIVE — UREA ON RICE
personaAdvisory.recommendation: HOLD urea unless severe N-deficiency confirmed. If needed, use light foliar spray (1%) or 5–8 kg/acre soil dose before morning irrigation. Avoid broadcast during flowering.
